title: NMR spectroscopic characterization of perioperative changes in the human metabolome during partial liver resection
summary:
This study investigates whether a special analysis method — called nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR) — can detect changes in the blood that indicate a risk of complications after liver surgery.
No extra blood samples are taken for this purpose: the study uses only leftover material from routine clinical blood tests, such as those performed for blood gas analysis.
The goal is to determine whether certain metabolic “fingerprints” in the blood can be identified that could warn of postoperative liver dysfunction or other complications at an early stage.
In the long run, this knowledge could help doctors better assess individual risk, detect complications earlier, and improve patient outcomes.
Participation in the study is voluntary and does not affect medical care. Patients can withdraw their consent at any time without any disadvantages.
